title: Nutty Velvety Middle Eastern Chestnuts Shakshuka
description: A bitter and velvety Middle Eastern dish featuring chestnuts, salt-bake, and Buddhist-temple-friendly ingredients, served in a shakshuka form on a salt block vessel.
instructions: Preheat the salt block vessel to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, toss the chopped chestnuts with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, paprika, cumin, salt, and black pepper until they are evenly coated.
Spread the chestnuts on the preheated salt block vessel and roast for 20 minutes.
In a large skillet, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onions to the skillet and cook until they are softened and translucent.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato puree and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Create 4 wells in the tomato mixture and crack an egg into each well.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake at 375 degrees Fahrenheit for 15 minutes.
Remove the skillet from the oven and top with the roasted chestnuts.
